analysis.investment_thesis: Meesho has genuine Tier-2/3 India consumption tailwinds with ~28% revenue CAGR (FY23-25), but the catastrophic net loss explosion to -3,942 Cr in FY25 (from -328 Cr in FY24) and promoter holding of just 16.57% make this uninvestable at 50x book for a loss-making subsidiary. Until the path to profitability is clear and governance improves, this is speculation, not investing.
key_strengths: Revenue growing strongly at ~28% CAGR (₹5,735 Cr → ₹9,390 Cr), targeting India's underpenetrated Tier-2/3 consumption boom
Asset-light marketplace model with 92% gross margins and minimal debt (D/E 0.09)
Operating cash flow turned positive at +₹539 Cr in FY25 with FCF of +₹516 Cr — unit economics improving at transaction level
key_risks: Promoter holding only 16.57% — no founder skin in the game, minority shareholders exposed with no alignment
EBITDA collapsed to -₹1,002 Cr in FY25 vs -₹281 Cr in FY24 — operating losses widening despite revenue scale
Intense competition from Flipkart, Amazon, and Myntra with deeper pockets makes durable moat very hard to build
red_flags: Meesho Ltd is a subsidiary of Meesho Inc (US entity) — Indian minority shareholders are structurally subordinate
Net loss exploded to -₹3,942 Cr in FY25 from -₹328 Cr in FY24 — a 12x deterioration in a single year
Other income swung from +₹231 Cr to -₹835 Cr — suggests massive write-downs or investment impairments not explained clearly
P/B of 50.42x on a company with steadily eroding equity (₹2,472 Cr → ₹1,446 Cr in two years)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Meesho is a genuine India internet-retail story targeting the largely untapped Tier-2 and Tier-3 consumer — a theme I believe in deeply. Revenue has grown from ₹5,735 Cr to ₹9,390 Cr in two years, OCF has turned positive, and the marketplace collects essentially zero inventory risk. These are real positives. But the FY25 numbers are deeply troubling: EBITDA deteriorated sharply to -₹1,002 Cr despite adding ₹1,775 Cr of revenue, and the net loss ballooned to -₹3,942 Cr — partly because "other income" swung by ₹1,066 Cr into negative territory. Something material happened on the balance sheet that is not transparent, and that opacity alone is disqualifying for me.

The governance structure is my biggest concern. A promoter holding of just 16.57% in what is formally a subsidiary of a US holding company means Indian public shareholders are structurally second-class. I've always said in India the promoter is everything — when he owns only 16%, his interests may diverge sharply from yours. At P/S of 6.5x and P/B of 50x for a company burning equity at this pace, the market is pricing in a future that the current fundamentals do not support. I need to see at least two consecutive years of EBITDA breakeven, promoter holding above 40%, and clarity on what caused the FY25 loss explosion before this becomes worth serious attention.
